item.title: Self hosted
item.description:
Container Usage

The application can run without copying config.yaml into the container. If no config file exists, it will automatically create one with sensible defaults.

item.title: Library
item.description: The Library is the heart of Soulsolid: it’s your music collection once it has been imported. Everything else in the app (importing, downloading, tagging, lyrics) ends up here, and the Library section is where you browse, search, inspect and clean it up.

item.title: Configuration
item.description:
The config.yaml file contains all application settings. Key sections:

  • libraryPath / downloadPath: Where the library lives and where downloads land
  • import: Import settings and file organization rules (see Importing and Paths)
  • metadata: Metadata provider settings (musicbrainz, deezer, discogs, acoustid)
  • lyrics: Lyrics provider settings (see Lyrics)
  • downloaders: External service configurations in the form of plugins. Supports both local .so files and automatic building from Git repositories (see Downloading)
  • jobs: Job logs and webhooks (see Jobs)
  • server, database, logger: Web server port, SQLite path and logging
  • telegram: Bot configuration and allowed users (deprecated, will be removed in v0.30.0)

Security Note: Never commit sensitive values like tokens or API keys to version control. Use environment variables or secret files instead.

item.title: Downloading
item.description: The Download section lets you search external music services and download tracks, albums, whole artists and playlists. Soulsolid doesn’t come with any music service built in: each service is added through a downloader plugin, so what you can search and download depends on the plugins you have configured. See Downloading for how to install one.

item.title: Importing
item.description: Importing is how music gets into your library. Point Soulsolid at a folder and it reads each file’s tags, checks whether you already have the song, organizes the file into your library folder and adds it to the library. Anything that needs your decision, such as a duplicate or a track with missing tags, is held in a review queue instead of being imported blindly.

item.title: Paths
item.description: Path templates decide where each track is placed in your library folder, based on its tags. This page describes the placeholders and functions you can use in them. Templates are used both when importing and when reorganizing your library.

item.title: Importing
item.description: Soulsolid imports music from folders on the server. When importing, it reads each file’s tags, checks whether you already have the song, moves or copies the file into your library folder, and creates artists and albums as needed.

item.title: Metadata / Tagging
item.description: The tag editor is where you view and fix a track’s tags. You can edit them by hand, or pull metadata from online providers (MusicBrainz, Discogs and Deezer) and review it before saving. Soulsolid can also identify tracks by how they sound using AcoustID, either one track at a time or for your whole library.

item.title: Downloading
item.description: Soulsolid can download music from online music services through downloader plugins. Soulsolid itself isn’t tied to any service: each service is supported by its own plugin, which you add to your configuration. Anyone can write a plugin for a new service (see the Plugin Development Guide).

item.title: Lyrics
item.description: Soulsolid can find lyrics for your tracks and save them into the audio files, so any player that reads embedded lyrics can show them. You can fetch lyrics for one track from the tag editor, or run a lyrics analysis over your whole library. Because lyrics you’ve curated by hand are easy to lose, Soulsolid never overwrites existing lyrics without asking: anything unclear goes to a review queue.
